programs.title: Attenborough's Wonder of Eggs
programs.desc: Bird eggs nurture new life, protecting it from the outside world while allowing it to breathe.They are strong enough not to break under the full weight of the incubating parent, and fragile enough for the chick to escape.From creation to hatching, Sir David Attenborough reveals the rich process behind these natural wonders.Along the way, he shares stories about the eggs of a whole range of birds - from swans and their aquatic world, to the cliffs where the common guillemot lives and lays its eggs.

programs.title: Attenborough's Wonder of Song
programs.desc: Sir David Attenborough selects seven of the most extraordinary recordings from the natural world and explores what these sounds mean to specific animal species.Each song - from that of a lemur, through the song of a humpback whale or a lyrebird from the order of passerine birds - was recorded during the lifetime of a famous naturalist who recorded and analyzed these songs for decades.The oldest recording was made when Sir David was five years old, the latest just a few years before the documentary was created.Each has an amazing story behind it and shows how much we still don't know about the natural world.When Sir David Attenborough was born, the science of song was transformed under Charles Darwin's theory of sexual selection, which labeled singing dangerous because it revealed the singer's location to predators.The same singing also gives males a great chance to be noticed by the female, and thus to pass on their genes to the next bird generation.So the males sing, and the females listen and choose the best singers because, according to them, they will be the best fathers.New scientific trends in bird song are challenging these long-held ideas.Scientists invited to the program show that in fact, in most species of songbirds, females create their own songs - and only now do they have a chance to be truly heard.However, there is a concern as to whether we will be able to learn all the songs of these extraordinary birds - the human loss is loud and the planet Earth is falling silently, as the host of the program also warns.The production is a continuation of the Grierson Award-nominated documentary "The Egg: A Miracle of Nature".

programs.title: Life Below Zero: The Thaw
programs.desc: Alaskans are preparing for a thaw.Snow-covered peaks turn into obstacle courses.Hikers encounter rushing streams and hungry predators and swarms of insects.

programs.title: Changing Planet: Coral Special
programs.desc: The special episode presents the behind-the-scenes of the mission.Three years after the project began, research into the problems of our planet's endangered ecosystems is still ongoing.Dr. M. Sanjayan visits the Maldives.

programs.title: Once Upon A Time In Space
Wonders of the Human Body with Michael Mosley
programs.desc: Using the latest achievements in science and medicine, host Michael Mosley delves into the interior of the human body to discover its secrets.In each episode, he explores new discoveries that significantly change our perception.From the possibility of 3D printing organs to gene therapies promising to reverse blindness.Throughout the series, he provides additional information in his characteristic way, offering his body to perform groundbreaking demonstrations.Created by an award-winning team, the series is full of visuals and fascinating facts.
